In this section we develop a novel probabilistic hybrid-peeling algorithm, 
denoted by~\texttt{HybridPeel}\xspace, 
which combines the randomized batch-peeling technique of \texttt{Prob\-Peel}\xspace (to overcome full enumeration of $\mathcal{S}_T$)
with a more refined peeling approach that peels vertices one at a time, to obtain higher quality solutions (as in \cite{Charikar2000}).

conclusions: With probability at least 1-eta, HybridPeelxspace is a frac(1-varepsilon)^2k(1+xi)(1+varepsilon)^2-approximation algorithm for the TMDSxspace~problem when J>1, while for J=1 it achieves a frac(1-varepsilon)^2k(1+xi)(1+varepsilon)-approximation ratio.

\label{lemma:ratioHybrid}
	With probability at least $1-\eta$, \texttt{HybridPeel}\xspace is a

\label{lemma:staticvstemporal}
	Given a temporal network $T=(V_T,E_T)$, and its associated directed network $D_{T}$, let $H^*$ be a solution to S2DS on~$D_{T}$. 
	Let $W^*$ on~$T$ be the optimal solution of~{TMDS}\xspace, for a 2-path motif, with fixed $\delta\ge 1$.
	Then there exists a temporal network $T$ such that $\ensuremath{\rho}\xspace(H^*)=0$ while $\ensuremath{\rho}\xspace(W^*) = \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\xspace(n^2)$.
	
	
	Furthermore, the two solution sets~$H^*$ and $W^*$ are~disjoint.

	Solving for $x$ in the equation
	\[
	n \frac{1}{(1+\xi)^x} = \ensuremath{\mathcal{O}}\xspace(1),
	\]
	proves the claim.
